scope: NCollection_Array1/Array2 CopyValues copy-assignment-only element policy and failure ordering
integration_status: committed candidate; root integration and cleanup pending

candidate_bindings.domain: Initialized owned or exclusively borrowed target storage, a disjoint source array, explicit copy assignment without Clone/copy construction, native shape and flat length validation, partial failure prefix and returned receiver identity.

Initialized owned or exclusively borrowed target storage, a disjoint source array, explicit copy assignment without Clone/copy construction, native shape and flat length validation, partial failure prefix and returned receiver identity.

initial_fixture_correction: The first Rust/Miri build rejected the test enum pattern Self::Matrix(donors), which unnecessarily fixed the donor storage lifetime to the receiver lifetime. Changing only the fixture pattern to CopyArray::Matrix retained independent borrow lifetimes. Production signatures were unchanged. Both initial compiler logs and final green runs are archived.
changes: Add two copy_values_with_assignment methods with stateful FnMut element assignment and no Clone or Default requirement.
Share native dimensional validation and storage access through Array1. Array2 first validates its rectangle, then validates and copies its inherited flat Array1 length.
Visit source/target pairs in increasing storage order, preserving the target prefix and failing-slot mutations after callback panic while retaining bounds, allocation and source values.
Return the existing receiver on success. Preserve caller-owned and mutable-borrowed storage; disjoint source/target views may occupy the same allocation.

Keep the existing Array1 Clone convenience method on slice clone_from_slice through a shared storage-policy engine, preserving its existing specialization semantics. Array2 convenience behavior and returning wrappers remain unchanged.
probe_policy: The native AssignOnlyItem deletes copy construction and records Q assignments and X destruction; the Rust payload omits Clone. Twenty-four rows exercise both array dimensions and every combination of owned/borrowed source/target for success and early/late failure. Two rows cover disjoint same-allocation views. Three mismatch rows discriminate native Array2 shape checking before Array1 length checking. Three rows cover actual flat extents of 0/2/5 for a four-cell rectangle. Ten tests consume all 32 rows; two Rust-only tests prove non-Default/non-Clone payload support and stateful callbacks.
limitations: The explicit callback chooses the native element assignment policy. It does not automatically infer arbitrary C++ overloads or triviality traits; existing Clone convenience and explicit trivial-copy APIs keep their separate policies.

Safe source and target borrows must be disjoint. Native nontrivial overlapping wrappers, element aliasing across source/target arrays, callback reentry and retained raw aliases remain outside this interface.
Native self CopyValues returns immediately without callbacks. Existing assign_self represents that receiver no-op; the new two-borrow callback method does not provide a same-receiver alias protocol.

Shared read-only targets retain existing detachment-on-mutation behavior. Native writable const-reference buffer aliases are not represented. Owned and mutable-borrowed domains do not incur Clone construction or detachment.

Equal rectangular dimensions with equal but independently changed flat lengths are defined for native CopyValues and covered. Unequal flat lengths reject before access. Uninitialized elements, allocation policy and ABI are not proved.
Rust panic/native exception observations cover assignment order, receiver/source state and defined lifetime events. Panicking Drop and native throwing-destructor termination are outside this slice.

All original assertions and prior array callback policies remain covered by cumulative regressions and strict Miri. The two bindings are partial-domain additions and do not close either class or add global inventory/legacy mapping credit.
